clue.text: One may correct a wrong author when speaking out

indicators.note: speaking out means the word for author is to be heard, not read, so its sound gives the letters

parts.note: an author is a writer

explanation.surface: Someone corrects an author who is giving a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One may correct a wrong' looks like a description of an editor, but it is the definition: a person who puts wrongs right.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sets wrongs straight is literally one who rights them, a redresser.

clue.text: Tyrannical nurse that's cut, namely abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means the abbreviation for namely is dropped from the longer word

parts.note: something cut, as by a claw, is scratched
sc. (scilicet) is the abbreviation for namely

explanation.surface: A bullying nurse who was hurt is left on her own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' takes SC out of SCRATCHED. SC (scilicet) means 'namely' in footnotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurse Ratched is the domineering ward nurse in One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest.

clue.text: Book Isaiah's leaving do?

definitions.meaning: Christopher Isherwood's 1939 novel of Weimar Berlin
a farewell party for the philosopher Isaiah Berlin would be a send-off to him

explanation.surface: A book of the prophet Isaiah describes a farewell party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' with 'Isaiah' suggests the Bible, but Isaiah is Sir Isaiah Berlin, the philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Isherwood's book title, read literally, is a send-off for anyone surnamed Berlin.

clue.text: Ode about a university's mutton stew

indicators.note: stew means the letters are stirred together into a new order

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A poem about a college's lamb casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' looks like the food the ode is about; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's ode on the season of mists and mellow fruitfulness is one of his great odes.

clue.text: Frost's archaic piece of verse

definitions.meaning: frost is, read as hoar frost, frozen dew on grass
an old spelling of rhyme, as in Coleridge's Ancient Mariner

explanation.surface: Robert Frost wrote an old-fashioned poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' looks like the poet Robert Frost; it is hoar frost, and the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoar frost is a white icy coating, and the same word was an old spelling of rhyme.

clue.text: Fool in one part of a book or another

indicators.note: in means the word for fool sits inside the word for a part of a book

parts.note: a page is one part of a book
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool appears in one section of a book or another.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the clue's 'part of a book': 'another' means another such part.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract or section of text in a book is another kind of book part.

clue.text: Heartless shelling stopped by actors making a web series

indicators.note: stopped by means the actors plug the gap inside the shelling word
heartless means the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: podding is shelling peas or beans
the cast are the actors

explanation.surface: Without mercy, a bombardment is halted by performers filming an online show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelling' reads as bombardment but means podding peas; 'Heartless' drops its middle D, leaving PODING for CAST to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Producing a series of audio episodes for online listeners is making a web series.

clue.text: Pool curing blindness,

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Pool curing blindness,' ends on a comma, so it is cut short; no scan, and searching was refused this run, so the wordplay cannot be recovered

clue.text: Cryptic clue for 'ardened detective's debut

parts.note: the title, read as a clue's instructions, says put A, then a study (DEN) inside scarlet (RED), building A R-DEN-ED, the word 'ardened

explanation.surface: A puzzle clue for a Cockney 'hardened' detective's first case.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as instructions, builds the clue word. A + DEN (study) inside RED (scarlet) makes ARDENED.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's 1887 novel is the first Sherlock Holmes story.

clue.text: Umberto Saba's last work originally owned by Hemingway?

parts.note: Ernest Hemingway, the American novelist

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The Italian poet's final book once belonged to Hemingway.
explanation.walkthrough: The ? marks the joke: a book owned by Ernest would be Ernest's 'O'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saba's novel Ernesto, written in 1953 and left unfinished, was his last work, published after his death.

clue.text: Playwright putting heart and weight behind Dylan?

indicators.note: behind means the other pieces follow after the name suggested by Dylan

parts.note: Dylan Thomas, the Welsh poet; the question mark flags a first name standing for a surname
the heart of something is its middle
a ton is a weight

explanation.surface: A dramatist backs Dylan with passion and heft.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jacobean dramatist who wrote The Changeling and Women Beware Women.

clue.text: Practices a part in Hair shyly at first

indicators.note: in means a small part is placed inside the opening letters
at first means only the opening letter of each of the two words is used

parts.note: a bit is a part

explanation.surface: Someone rehearses a small role in the musical Hair, timidly at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Hair is the 1960s rock musical; it looks like a stage cue but only gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Customs or routines a person regularly follows are their usual practices.

clue.text: They murdered grooms and butchered attendants

indicators.note: butchered means the letters of the two words before it are hacked into a new order

parts.note: aides are attendants

explanation.surface: A gruesome crime scene where bridegrooms and their servants were slaughtered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grooms' suggests Macbeth's murdered grooms, but these are bridegrooms. In Greek myth the daughters of Danaus killed their husbands on the wedding night.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the fifty daughters of Danaus killed their bridegrooms on their wedding night.

clue.text: Place to go without water and study a poet

parts.note: the john is slang for a lavatory
dry means without water
a den is a study

explanation.surface: Someone goes to a desert place to study a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Restoration poet laureate who wrote Absalom and Achitophel.

clue.text: Best Drama Oscar designed for heartthrobs

indicators.note: designed means the letters are worked into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: The Academy Award for best drama goes to the film stars women swoon over.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractive people others swoon over are dreamy idols, objects of romantic longing.

clue.text: Achieved nothing in relation to Pygmalion

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase: a relative of Pygmalion, king of Tyre

parts.note: achieved means did
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone made no headway with Shaw's play Pygmalion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in relation to' reads as 'concerning', but it means 'a relation of': the queen of Carthage was the sister of Pygmalion of Tyre, not Shaw's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder-queen of Carthage was the sister of Pygmalion, king of Tyre, so his relation.

clue.text: It's loaded, fabulous, and full of gold

definitions.text: It's loaded, fabulous, and full of gold

parts.words: It's loaded, fabulous, and full of gold
parts.note: reads as praise of a rich person, but describes the legendary South American city of gold

explanation.surface: A gushing description of a very rich person.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary city of the Americas sought by conquistadors was fabled to be rich in gold.

clue.text: Oberon's one low note

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

explanation.surface: The fairy king Oberon has a single deep note.
explanation.walkthrough: Oberon is Shakespeare's fairy king, but here he is a satellite of Uranus, so 'Oberon's one' is the kind of body Oberon is.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon is one of the satellites of the planet Uranus.

clue.text: Unfinished wine one's taken into large stage show

indicators.note: taken into means one is placed inside the shortened wine
unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: muscat is a sweet wine
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A half-drunk wine is carried into a big theatre production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfinished' cuts MUSCAT to MUSCA; I goes inside, then L.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre production built on songs and dance numbers is a sung stage show.

clue.text: Novel lone dunces penned? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of the two words take a new order

explanation.surface: A novel about lonely fools kept in an enclosure, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book in a literary puzzle; it is the anagram signal. The definition is the opposite of 'penned' (shut in).
explanation.definitionFit: Not shut in or fenced around, the reverse of being kept in a pen.

clue.text: Haze, maybe of grief, ends in three suicides

parts.note: dolor is grief or sorrow

indicators.note: ends in means the last letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A fog, perhaps of grief, ends in three suicides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haze' looks like mist; it is Dolores Haze, Nabokov's Lolita.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolores Haze is the full name of the girl in Nabokov's novel Lolita.

clue.text: Group including Ruth regularly upset Silvia's suitor

indicators.note: including means the group holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a trio is a group of three

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the picked letters are turned upside down
regularly means every other letter of the name

explanation.surface: A band that includes Ruth gets in a state over a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Silvia is the heroine of Shakespeare's The Two Gentlemen of Verona; in a down clue 'upset' turns the picked letters over.
explanation.definitionFit: Thurio is the foolish rival suitor for Silvia in The Two Gentlemen of Verona.

clue.text: Hut housing quiet female's Nan who wrote The Weatherhouse

indicators.note: housing means the hut holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a shed is a hut
p (piano) is the musical direction for quiet
her is the female possessive

explanation.surface: A grandmother lives in a hut, with a silent woman, and wrote a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nan' reads as a grandmother but is the Scottish writer's first name; her novel The Weatherhouse appeared in 1930.
explanation.definitionFit: Nan Shepherd, the Scottish author of The Living Mountain, also wrote the novel The Weatherhouse.

clue.text: Majestic lawn's opening for Charity in Summer

parts.note: majestic means royal

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A grand lawn opens for a charity event in summertime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charity in Summer' sounds like a fete, but Summer is Edith Wharton's 1917 novel and Charity its heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity Royall is the heroine of Edith Wharton's novel Summer.

clue.text: He's going to where Dante went

definitions.meaning: he will, contracted, said of a man about to act
Dante's Inferno describes his journey through the underworld of the damned

explanation.surface: A man is going to the place Dante visited.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inferno has Dante touring the infernal regions, and 'he will' contracts to the same letters.

clue.text: Poet, Good writer and composer

parts.note: Samuel Taylor Coleridge, the Romantic poet
C. P. Taylor wrote the play Good (1981)

explanation.surface: A list of three people: a poet, a fine writer, and a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good writer' looks like praise, but Good is the title of a play by C. P. Taylor.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Coleridge-Taylor was an English composer, best known for Hiawatha's Wedding Feast.

clue.text: Lawyer in Michael Connelly's city

definitions.meaning: Connelly's novel The ... Lawyer names its hero after the car he works from
the cathedral city in the East Midlands of England, or the capital of Nebraska

explanation.surface: A lawyer works in the city where the crime novelist sets his books.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Connelly's city looks like Los Angeles, but the word is the one before 'Lawyer' in his title.
explanation.definitionFit: The title The Lincoln Lawyer pairs the word with the lawyer; it is also an English cathedral city.

clue.text: Coward, perhaps retreating with group backing a paranoid king

indicators.note: retreating means the first name is read backwards

parts.note: Noel Coward, the playwright; perhaps flags a first name by example

indicators.note: backing means the group word is read backwards too

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A coward backs away and his gang supports a suspicious monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' is the playwright Noel Coward, not a timid person; the paranoid king is from Shakespeare's The Winter's Tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Sicilia in The Winter's Tale is consumed by groundless jealousy of his wife.
